en.name: Brown rice
en.summary: Brown rice still has its bran and germ, which is why it is worth eating and why it does not keep like white rice. Sealed in a cupboard it runs about 1 year from purchase and about 1 year from opening; refrigerated after opening, about 6 months.
en.pantry: An airtight container in a cool, dark, dry cupboard gives about 1 year from purchase, and about 1 year again from the day you open the bag if you decant it properly. The bran layer carries oil, and that oil oxidises — which is why brown rice goes bitter and slightly stale-smelling while white rice from the same harvest is still fine. Paper sacks are no barrier to rice weevils, so decant. Keep it away from the hob and out of sunlight, and buy the bag size you will actually finish.
en.fridge: An airtight container in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below gives about 6 months after opening, and in a hot, humid climate that is the sensible choice for brown rice specifically — cold slows the bran oil from turning and deals with weevils at the same time. Seal it well, because rice takes up fridge smells, and let the container come back to room temperature before opening so condensation forms on the outside rather than on the grain. Cooked rice is an entirely different matter and belongs in a shallow container, chilled fast.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for brown rice here, so none is given. Freezing a sealed bag for a few days is a reliable way to kill weevil eggs, and long freezing does slow rancidity, but neither is a documented shelf life. If you buy brown rice in bulk, the refrigerated figure is the useful one to plan around; if you have more than that, buy less next time rather than filling a freezer.
spoilage: A bitter, oily or paint-like smell — the bran oil has turned, and this is how brown rice usually ends.
A musty smell, which means damp and probably mould; do not wash it and cook it anyway.
Live weevils, small moths, webbing or fine powdery dust.
Cooked rice that tastes bitter or stale however it is seasoned.
tips: Decant into an airtight container the day you buy it.
Keep an opened bag in the fridge through a humid summer.
Smell the dry grain before cooking; rancidity does not show.
Buy smaller bags than you would of white rice — it has a shorter life.

faq.q: How long does brown rice keep?
faq.a: About 1 year from purchase and about 1 year from opening in an airtight cupboard container, or about 6 months refrigerated after opening.

faq.q: Why does brown rice keep less time than white?
faq.a: Because the bran and germ are still on it, and the oil they contain goes rancid. Milling removes both from white rice.

faq.q: Should brown rice be kept in the fridge?
faq.a: In a hot, humid kitchen, yes — an airtight container at 4 °C (40 °F) or below slows the bran oil turning and keeps weevils out.

zh.name: 糙米
zh.summary: 糙米保留了麩皮和胚芽，那既是吃它的理由，也是它無法像白米那樣耐放的原因。密封放櫥櫃從購買日起算約 1 年，開封後約 1 年；開封後冷藏約 6 個月。
zh.pantry: 密封容器放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 1 年；只要一開封就確實換裝，開封後同樣約 1 年。麩皮層含油，而那些油會氧化——這就是為什麼同一批收成的米，糙米已經發苦帶陳味，白米卻還好好的。紙袋擋不住米象，所以一定要換裝。遠離爐台、避免陽光直射，並且買你真的吃得完的份量。
zh.fridge: 密封容器放 4 °C 以下，開封後約 6 個月；在濕熱氣候下，這對糙米來說是特別合理的選擇——低溫同時延緩麩皮油脂變質並解決米象。密封要確實，因為米很會吸冰箱的味道；開封前先讓容器回到室溫，讓水氣凝在外面而不是米上。煮熟的飯則完全是另一回事，要裝淺容器快速冷卻。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給糙米的冷凍期限，所以本頁不給。把密封袋冷凍幾天是殺死蟲卵的可靠方法，長期冷凍也確實能延緩油耗，但兩者都不是有出處的保存期限。如果你大量買糙米，冷藏那個數字才是規劃的依據；如果連那也吃不完，下次少買一點，不要把冷凍庫塞滿。
spoilage: 聞起來發苦、油味重或有油漆味——麩皮油脂變質，這也是糙米最常見的結局。
聞到霉味，代表受潮、多半已經發霉；不要洗一洗照樣煮。
看到活的米象、小蛾、絲網或細粉屑。
煮出來的飯不管怎麼調味都苦或陳。
tips: 買回來當天就倒進密封容器。
潮濕的夏天，開封後那一包請放冰箱。
煮之前先聞生米；油耗是看不出來的。
比白米買更小包——它的壽命本來就比較短。

faq.a: 密封放櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 1 年、開封後約 1 年；開封後冷藏約 6 個月。

faq.q: 為什麼糙米比白米不耐放？
faq.a: 因為它還帶著麩皮和胚芽，裡面的油脂會走油耗。白米在碾製時已經把兩者去掉了。
在濕熱的廚房裡建議放。密封容器、4 °C 以下，可以延緩麩皮油脂變質，也擋得住米象。
